statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail remains at 24 because the verified Kharg tanker strike and continuing Gulf supply disruption raise reopening-gap sensitivity, while the weekend NQ closure prevents confirmation of persistent Nasdaq price-path failure.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: WATCH; Tail remains below the block threshold. Stress is extreme from Gulf, energy-price and rate risks, while no live Nasdaq continuation or failed-retracement structure is observable during the weekend closure.
headline: Kharg discontinuity keeps closed-market Nasdaq regime at WATCH
body: The reported U.S. strike on an Iranian tanker near Kharg Island remains the main discontinuity risk. Friday's strong payroll report and higher yields reinforce macro Stress, while elevated oil and constrained Hormuz traffic add supply risk. NQ is closed, so no live persistent mean-reversion failure can be established.

lookbackSummary: The prior 24 hours include Friday's post-payroll repricing, two brief orange Tail episodes during live trading, the transition into weekend closure, and a return to WATCH after the Kharg tanker-strike report. Since NQ closed, Tail has been driven by discontinuity risk rather than observed persistent mean-reversion failure.
outlookSummary: NQ remains closed throughout this 24-hour horizon. If no additional verified Gulf escalation or material Hormuz deterioration appears, Tail is projected to ease gradually within WATCH as the Kharg shock ages; Stress remains extreme from conflict, energy costs and rate pressure while confidence declines as Friday's live evidence becomes older.
